title: Base and Balance
shortDefinition: Base is the ability to keep center of gravity while staying mobile and reactive.
whyItMatters: Without base, you get swept, snapped down, off-balanced, or lose pressure when changing direction.
deepExplanation: Good base is not stiffness. It is weight distribution, active toes, knee width, and head-hip alignment suited to the phase.
beginnerView: Do not need both hands posted for long to stay balanced.
advancedView: Let the opponent feel they can off-balance, then redirect into a counter.

ifThenExamples.if: If you lose Base and Balance during the exchange.
ifThenExamples.then: Stop accelerating, recover the nearest body structure, then continue the technique.
ifThenExamples.why: Modern no-gi punishes forceful continuation after structure is lost.

ifThenExamples.if: If the opponent correctly answers your first line.
ifThenExamples.then: Use Base and Balance to switch to a safer branch instead of forcing the same line.
ifThenExamples.why: A good concept turns the opponent’s reaction into information for the next decision.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Base and Balance is a single technical trick.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: Treat it as a decision rule that appears across many positions.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Understanding the concept automatically makes it work live.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: The concept needs body signals, short cues, and positional rolling.

trainingCues: Name Base and Balance before adding force.
Find the body signal instead of guessing generally.
If structure is lost, reset one layer first.
Drill slowly, then test with progressive resistance.
